text:
katya: Heads-up — ran microbatch window sweep on canary cluster. Observed p99 token latency up ~8-12% vs baseline when micro_interval_ms <= 4ms and using the new fused-attn kernel.
omar: Oof. Any KV cache metrics?
katya: KV miss rate climbed from ~2.1% to ~6.8% (short windows -> more eviction churn). Also saw more small batches hitting kernel warmup.
max: Do you have the profiling dump? CPU vs GPU breakdown?
katya: Pasted top-of-stack sample from pprof for the slow run:
```
CPU: fused_attn_kernel_wrapper (30%)
CPU: microbatch_coalesce_loop (18%)
CPU: kv_cache_lookup (12%)
GPU kernel time: fused_attn (55% of GPU time)
Small-batch overhead: ~22us per request
```
teresa: Sounds like two interacting effects: smaller micro_interval increases batch formation churn, and fused-attn has worse warmup cost for tiny seq lengths. We need to tune jitter and token_budget to avoid mini-batches.
lee: Quick thought — increase jitter P95 so arrivals spread, and set token_budget target to prefer merging short requests. Example config to try: 
```yaml
microbatch:
  micro_interval_ms: 3
  coalesce_delay_ms: 2
  jitter_p50_ms: 1.0
  jitter_p95_ms: 6.0
queue_policy: 
  type: priority-bound
  small_request_threshold: 64
token_budget:
  target_per_batch: 8192
  min_batch_tokens: 256
```
omar: I like raising token target to 8192 for the canary; forces the runtime to wait for more tokens up to SLA. But watch tail latency for long requests.
perf-bot: :bar_chart: perf/regression detected on canary after deploy 2024-11-07T14:12Z — p99 token latency +9.7% (compared to baseline). Related: fused-attn kernel variant.
max: Proposed A/B experiment: group A (current fused-attn + micro_interval=3/jitter_p95=2), group B (fused-attn + micro_interval=3/jitter_p95=6 + token_target=8192). Collect p50/p95/p99, KV miss rate, avg batch size, kernel warmup counts for 2h.
katya: I'll kick off patches and add extra instrumentation: emit batch_size histogram with seq_len buckets, and record kernel_warmup_count per shard.
lee: Also capture per-route SLA regressions, and add fallback rule: if p99 increases >5% for route* then fallback to legacy-attn kernel automatically.
teresa: Can we also simulate synthetic load with mix of short (16-64) and long (512+) sequences? We should reproduce locally before canary.
katya: Good call — I'll run a 30m synthetic run with 70/30 short/long and export traces.
omar: If the KV miss is main culprit we could try gentler eviction (LRU window extension) or pre-priming KV for hot prefixes. But that's a separate change.
max: For immediate triage: run A/B, gather profiles, then decide — either relax micro_interval or add token_budget increase + jitter tweak.
katya: Assigned: katya will run synthetic and A/B, lee will add automatic fallback, teresa will craft fallback criteria, max will own perf comparisons. Sync in 2h. :rocket:
omar: Ack.
perf-bot: :white_check_mark: experiment started: /experiments/1715014327-microbatch-window-swing (canary A/B).
